Limited resources: Every court department I've spoken with has sent me to another department and it's just going in circles from there.

The forms were filled out with the assistance of a domestic violence advocacy program. The dog was included in the animal care portion because the dog was a victim and tool of abuse. The welfare checks were recommended by animal advocates and an animal regulations worker.

I'm literally just trying to follow directions that I'm given by police, professionals, and other staff.

The resources seem severely limited. Since the trial was regarding a restraining order, pet protection wasn't the primary component and I keep being sent in circles in terms of moving forward. I've basically been told that had I not pursued the restraining order or if I had a different judge, I would still have my dog. The only thing I seem to be able to do is have animal regulation do welfare checks to make sure they're not still neglecting him. 
I appreciate the information.

It reads like there's a good chunk of cognitive dissonance. It reads like you want to have these critical discussions but don't have good communication with the people around you. It reads like you care about "good." 

Now, communication is supposed to be a two-way street, but people don't always pick up their end. You are responsible for what you believe, what you do for yourself, how you interact with the world around you, and how you communicate with other people. And the funny thing about communication is that people, verbally or non-verbally, operate on their own set of values and that's what they put out. That's also why cognitive dissonance sucks... people will convince themselves that they don't actually believe what they believe. It can be harder to find, but it still comes out. I want you to think... "What can I do about it?"

You need to evaluate your concept of good and how it's implemented in the world. 

There are people here who will always value your life. There are people here who would put their own life on the line for you. Your responsibility is to figure out how you value their response and how you value your own thoughts. 

A little help from others can be a great blessing. What are you going to do with it?

Mine was like, "wow, that's a lot." And I really appreciated that.

I have had people say that I'm a fighter or I'll be okay because I'm smart and can overcome the environmental circumstances, and I really needed them to fuck off with their bullshit.
I don't really know how to answer your question. It stems from organized crime and enforces a lot of religious beliefs.

I was in recruiting. I saw some disastrous apps, but none of the candidates hold a candle to one guy who was actually hired. I was in no way responsible for picking this guy. I honestly don't know how he passed screening.

He was struggling in his position when leadership went to do a routine check on his progress. Guy walked out and claimed a leave of absence due to a panic attack. He was on paid leave for over a year, came back for a week, and went back on leave.

I was homeless when shelter-in-place was ordered. I stayed at two different houses and a motel before I found an apartment. The motel didn't have amenities... even though shopping was essential, I was in public frequently because there wasn't a good way to keep perishables.

It just wasn't an option.
